conviction_note: Pre-revenue eVTOL developer with no options market and a thin, single-source EPS bar (-$0.08). What we found is mostly priced or small: a likely non-cash warrant fair-value gain that should make GAAP EPS look better than consensus (stock -43% from May 29 to Aug 31), a new $50m ATM opened Sep 4 into a stock that has since drifted -15% on rising volume, a guided spend step-up, and a business update whose public items (two LOIs) did not move the stock when announced. Findings net to -0.5. Scaled number: abs 9 (median prior reaction 8.65, max 16, thin turnover, no new guidance expected) times a 45% chance of a higher close (1 of 4 prior prints up, ATM overhang) = -0.9. The two measurements agree in sign and size; the EPS headline beat (print_vs_bar +40%) and the slightly negative reaction disagree on purpose, because this name trades on cash, dilution and milestones, not GAAP EPS, and the beat is a remeasurement.
bar: GAAP EPS consensus -$0.08 per share for fiscal Q1 2027, from one source only (Earnings Whispers, https://beta.earningswhispers.com/go/w/HOVR, undated page that confirms the 2026-10-09 bmo date). No company guide and no second agreeing estimate, so every finding that depends on it is capped small. No revenue bar (pre-revenue). The line the stock likely trades on is cash/burn and the business update, not EPS. Prior quarter: Q4 FY26 EPS about -$0.13 vs -$0.11 estimate per Benzinga (https://www.benzinga.com/quote/HOVR/earnings).
positioning_check: Short interest 2,726,039 shares, 4.57% of float, days to cover 4.4 at about 1.32m average volume, record date 2026-09-15, published 2026-09-24 (MarketBeat, https://www.marketbeat.com/stocks/NASDAQ/HOVR/short-interest/). Against the baseline's 20-day average volume of 416k it is about 6.5 days. Down 3.4% from the prior report. Not crowded, so it gives no squeeze reason to shrink the negatives. No options market, so no skew. Tape: spot $1.535, -8.1% over 5 sessions, -5.3% over 20, -60.7% from the 52-week high and 27.9% above the low. Volume roughly doubled Oct 5-7 (568k, 581k, 577k vs about 280-330k on Sep 28-Oct 2) as the stock went 1.68 -> 1.53 with no news found. Alyeska Investment Group holds 6.72% (13G, event 2026-06-30), partly through RDO pre-funded warrants.

findings.finding: GAAP net loss for Q1 FY27 (Jun-Aug 2026) will probably be much narrower than the -$0.08 consensus because of a non-cash warrant fair-value GAIN. The company carries warrant liabilities marked to the stock (FY26 fair-value loss CAD 10.80m; quarterly CAD +5.14m Q1, +3.99m Q2, -0.995m Q3, about +2.67m Q4), and HOVR fell from $2.93 (2026-05-29) to $1.67 (2026-08-31), -43%. Outstanding at May 31: 12,065,375 warrants at $11.50 plus RDO I/II and general warrants. In Q1 FY26 the same line ran the other way (a CAD 5.14m loss turned a CAD ~5.8m operating loss into -10.9m) and the stock fell 16% on that print.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q1 FY26 (2025-10-10): warrant loss, EPS reported as a miss (-0.16 vs -0.13 per aggregators), stock -16.08%, but it had risen 15.5% the day before. Q4 FY26 (2026-07-16): EPS -0.13 vs -0.11, a miss, stock -12.28%. The one up print (2026-01-14, +5.03%) followed Q2's CAD 3.99m warrant loss, so EPS headlines do not map cleanly to reactions.
findings.why_not_priced: Consensus -$0.08 (about USD 5.4m on 67m shares) looks like an operating-loss run-rate, i.e. about the Q4 FY26 loss with no remeasurement. If the warrant gain were modelled, the estimate would sit nearer -$0.02 to -$0.05. On a 1-2 analyst name nobody updates for it. It is a below-the-line remeasurement with no path to cash or the guide, so even if it lands, holders who look through it are right to.
findings.independence: Same-direction evidence from a different source: warrant count and $11.50 strike from the 10-K MD&A (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001930021/000121390026078490/ea0295260-10k_newhorizon.htm). The size of the gain is an inference: no warrant price for May 29 / Aug 31 could be sourced, and HOVRW traded $0.31 on 2026-10-07.

findings.finding: Financing: on 2026-09-04 the company filed a 424B5 for a new $50m at-the-market program with JonesTrading (up to 3% commission) under its $200m shelf (S-3, 2026-08-28). The last price in the filing was $1.81 on Aug 27, with 67,123,941 shares outstanding. That is about half the current ~$103m market cap, on top of 9.04m ATM shares sold in FY26 and two RDOs in May ($2.15 and $2.51). The stock is now $1.535 (-15% since the supplement) and volume doubled on Oct 5-7 with no news. The 10-Q cover share count and subsequent-events note will show how much was sold after Aug 31. The 10-K and the prospectus also say there is 'substantial doubt' about going concern beyond 12 months without more capital, against the press-release line of 'more than 24 months of liquidity'. What the money buys: the use of proceeds is aircraft development. That use is corroborated (RAMPF fuselage, BETA flight computers, headcount 56 -> 100+ by summer 2027), but it is a pre-revenue build with no backlog to fund, so the sign stays negative.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: May 2026 RDOs at $2.15 and $2.51 were followed by the stock sliding from $2.93 (May 29) to about $1.76 by July 10. The baseline does not isolate the reaction to dilution disclosures in a print.
findings.why_not_priced: The ATM's existence is public and the drift since Sep 4 probably reflects it. What is not public is how many shares were sold in Sep-Oct at $1.6-1.7. If heavy selling were known, the stock would already have reset on volume. Instead the selling looks gradual (Oct 5-7 volume about 2x the prior week). Light usage would be a mild relief.
findings.independence: Volume and price series from Yahoo (https://query1.finance.yahoo.com/v8/finance/chart/HOVR?range=10d&interval=1d). Going-concern wording from the 10-K (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001930021/000121390026078490/ea0295260-10k_newhorizon.htm). The prospectus and the 10-K are different documents but come from one issuer.

findings.finding: Cash burn will step up as guided. FY26 operating cash outflow was CAD 16.5m (quarters: 2.36, 2.61, 6.82, 4.70). The company guided that FY27 spend steps up as major components arrive and engineering headcount roughly doubles, while liquidity stays above 24 months. A Q1 FY27 outflow of CAD 6-9m would leave cash near CAD 70m against CAD 78.3m at May 31, before any ATM proceeds.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Not isolable. The July print (-12.28%) showed an FY burn of CAD 16m and the 24-month liquidity claim together.
findings.why_not_priced: It is largely priced: the step-up was guided on the July 16 call (https://quartr.com/events/new-horizon-aircraft-ltd-hovr-q4-2026_FRQBx1ni). Only a burn well above about CAD 9m a quarter would be news, and nothing was found pointing to that.
findings.independence: Guidance from the Quartr Q4 FY26 summary, a different source from the XBRL cash-flow data.

findings.finding: Demonstrator schedule risk in the business update. Aviation Week reported the full-scale Cavorite X7 demonstrator slipped about one quarter to spring 2027, which the company attributed to prioritising certification readiness. The July 16 release then said initial testing is on track for calendar Q1 2027. The update will either reaffirm the date or slip it again. Nothing found indicates a second slip.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The slip appears to have surfaced around the July FY print (-12.28%), but its share of that move cannot be separated out.
findings.source_date: 2026 (paywalled; summary only, exact date not confirmed from the page)
findings.why_not_priced: The first slip is priced. A second slip is a tail risk the stock, at a 60% drawdown, may partly carry already. A reaffirmation is the base case and is worth about zero.
findings.independence: The July 16 release's 'on track for initial testing in Q1 calendar 2027' (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1930021/000121390026078500/ea029810101ex99-1.htm) argues against a further slip. The finding is sized net of that.

findings.finding: Two non-binding LOIs to convert or recap in the business update: V-Star Powered Lift (2026-07-21, 5 firm plus 95 options, 'up to $600m', a deposit only when a definitive agreement is signed) and Great Lakes Helicopter (2026-09-29, MRO, pilot training and some aircraft purchases, no terms). The company named converting V-Star to a definitive agreement as its next goal. A signed definitive agreement with a deposit would be new; a recap would not.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The Great Lakes LOI on 2026-09-29 moved the stock 0.0% ($1.70 to $1.70). The V-Star LOI came after the July print, and the stock was about $1.97 by Aug 6.
findings.why_not_priced: Both LOIs are public and the Great Lakes one drew no reaction, so a recap is priced. Only a conversion to a definitive agreement with a deposit would be unpriced, and no evidence of one was found.
findings.independence: V-Star LOI release: https://www.newswire.com/news/horizon-aircraft-secures-loi-with-v-star-powered-lift-aviation-for-the-purchase. It is a separate document.

findings.finding: RDO holders sit under water. Alyeska Investment Group filed a 13G showing 6.72% (4,148,433 shares, including 2,160,897 via pre-funded warrants, event date 2026-06-30). Those positions came from the May registered directs at $2.15 and $2.51, and the stock is now $1.535. Shares outstanding rose from the 61.76m Alyeska used to 67.12m by Aug 27, consistent with pre-funded warrant exercises and ATM sales.
findings.why_not_priced: The holding is public. Whether Alyeska is a seller is an inference, and the drift since May would already reflect any selling.
findings.independence: The share count of 67,123,941 at Aug 27 comes from the 424B5 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1930021/000121390026097676/ea0304433-424b5_newhorizon.htm).

outside_window.finding: Full-scale Cavorite X7 demonstrator completion and initial ground testing, targeted spring / calendar Q1 2027.
The going-concern horizon. The 10-K says cash covers 'at least 12 months' with substantial doubt beyond that without new capital, so the question becomes binding around mid-2027.

baseline_tension: There is no skew. The slight negative lean agrees with the -8% five-day run-up and with 3 of 4 prior prints not up, so it is probably partly priced. The one positive (the EPS headline from the warrant gain) cuts against the tape but is a remeasurement.
lessons_applied: Lesson 2 (one-offs) and lesson 6 (single-source bar): warrant fair-value gain cut from +0.6 to +0.3. It is a below-the-line remeasurement with no path to the guide, sized against a one-source EPS bar.

Lesson 4 (financing is a question): asked what the ATM buys. The answer is a corroborated development build (suppliers, hiring), not a revenue ramp with backlog. The sign stays negative but is cut from -1.0 to -0.6.
Lesson 6 (inside guidance): burn step-up was guided in July, so it moves from -0.3 to -0.1.
Lesson 3 (own caveat): the demonstrator-slip finding's own independence (July 'on track') argues against it, so -0.3 becomes -0.2.
Lesson 5 (positioning and unexplained drawdown worth ~0): Alyeska RDO-holder finding moves from -0.2 to -0.1.
Lesson 8 / core 3b: abs_move_pct raised from 8 to 9 (thin turnover, hunters' numbers run small). p_up left at 45.
